    The loop quiver #

    The loop quiver •↺ has a single vertex and a single arrow from it to itself. It is the smallest quiver that is not acyclic, which makes it the standard boundary case of the theory: its path algebra is the infinite-dimensional k[X] (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.OneLoop.PathAlgebra), and it has infinite representation type over every field (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.OneLoop.FiniteRepType).

    This file defines the vertex and arrow data and classifies paths by their length, independently of the algebra and representation theory.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.OneLoop: the vertex type, a singleton, with a Quiver instance whose only arrow type is PUnit.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.OneLoop.loop: the unique arrow, from the vertex to itself.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.OneLoop.totalPathEquivNat: paths are classified by their length.
